decisions.reason: Separate control of LED and sensor power does not change the standalone USB power source, activation condition, capacity, or powered 3.3V scope.
The source does not change the boost converter's enable GPIO, output capacity, or supplied loads; separate LED and sensor control can coexist with the current 5V boost supply state.
The source concerns separate control of LED and sensor power, not selection or OR-ing of the two 3.3V power sources.
Separate load control does not alter the requirement to meter the 3.3V and 5V rails or the stated monitoring topology.
The source does not change how battery-charge status is displayed, the charge-status connector, or its component values.
The source does not add, remove, or redefine any main-board connector.
Although separate control could require control signals, the source assigns no GPIO and does not alter any existing GPIO mapping.
The source does not change the sensor-board input connectors, sensor output connectors, pinouts, or connector count.
Separate LED and sensor power control does not alter the requirement for main-board decoupling capacitors.
The source does not affect panel controls, touch inputs, reset wiring, button placement, or their connector-based implementation.
The source does not revise the interboard connector architecture, signal pinout, power signals, or matching-numbering requirement.
The source concerns LED and sensor power control and a possible LED level shifter, not I2C series-resistor values, placement, or population policy.
